title: Getter Requiring &mut self Only for Lazy Initialization
pattern: A logically read-only accessor takes `&mut self` solely so it can lazily initialize or cache a field on first use.
why_bad: The implementation detail leaks into the signature: callers need exclusive access to perform a read, so the value cannot be read through a shared reference, from several places at once, or across threads, and borrow-checker friction spreads `&mut` through code that never changes anything observable.
detection: A `get_*`/accessor method with a `&mut self` receiver whose only mutation is filling an `Option`/cache field (`if self.x.is_none() { self.x = Some(..) }`, `get_or_insert_with`) before returning it.
counterexample: Accessors whose initialization has observable effects or can fail and must be sequenced by the caller; types that are only ever used through unique ownership where `&mut` imposes no cost; interior mutability already in use (`OnceCell`, `OnceLock`, `LazyLock`, `RefCell`).
source: Michael Feathers, *Working Effectively with Legacy Code* (2004), Ch. 25; Jon Gjengset, *Rust for Rustaceans* (2021), Ch. 3.
